title: Kessler Shield Vehicle Service Contracts — Measuring Day of the Term on a Traded-Vehicle Refund
content:
**Rule.** For a traded-vehicle refund on a Kessler Shield Vehicle Service Contracts contract, the term is used up to a measuring day. The elapsed days run from the term start date to that day. The measuring day is the first of the following that applies:
1. **Kessler Care cancellation.** The Kessler Care plan sold on the contract's purchase deal is a Kessler Care Prepaid Maintenance Plans plan; a contract sold on its own has no such plan. Where that plan carries a refund calculated on a cancellation for the vehicle being sold or traded, dated after this contract's sale date and on or before the request date, the measuring day is the date of that refund calculation. Where several exist, the latest is used; on a same-day tie, the one listed first.
2. **GAP loan payoff.** Where none does, consider the GAP waiver sold on the contract's purchase deal; a contract sold on its own has none. Where it records the loan paid off on a date after this contract's sale date and on or before the request date, the measuring day is that payoff date. This is read from the Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda records.
3. **Otherwise,** the effective date.

**Boundary table (hypothetical; sale date 1 May of one year, request date 20 June of the next).**

| Kessler Care sold-or-traded refund calculation | GAP loan payoff | Measuring day |
|---|---|---|
| 2 June of the next year | 5 June of the next year | 2 June |
| 20 June of the next year (the request date) | — | 20 June |
| 21 June of the next year (after the request date) | 5 June of the next year | 5 June |
| 1 May (the sale date itself) | none | 20 June (the effective date) |
| none | none | 20 June (the effective date) |
